encyclopedia.summary: George Miller's 1981 sequel moves the series past the revenge story of the first film and onto the roads of a collapsed civilisation. Max drifts the wasteland looking for fuel and ends up siding with the people defending a refinery against a marauding gang. Its habit of carrying the story through the design of vehicle chases rather than dialogue set the grammar for post-apocalyptic cinema after it.
highlights: The final tanker chase runs twenty minutes on speed and impact with almost no dialogue.
The conflict is a community's survival over fuel and water, not the first film's police revenge.
Mad Max: Fury Road (2015) picks this film's world and chase grammar back up.

related.note: Later film in the same world, pushing the chase to its limit
Another wasteland action film of 1980s Hollywood

encyclopedia.summary: Thirty years after the Empire fell, the Resistance searches for a vanished Luke Skywalker while a scavenger on a desert world meets an old droid carrying part of a map. J.J. Abrams directed and Lucasfilm released it in 2015, opening a sequel trilogy that deliberately reuses the grammar of the original films.
highlights: It builds a new trio in Rey, Finn and Kylo Ren while pushing the original three into supporting roles.
Practical sets and miniatures return, giving it a texture the prequels had traded for CGI.
Reception split between fan service and reboot, but it put the series back at the centre of cinema.
